name: samba leko

catalog_locator: Ch. Phonologie, section 3 'LES TONS', printed p. 65-66 (p. 66-67); diachronic remark on p. 61 (p. 62)
catalog_quote: Le samba leko est une langue à trois hauteurs tonales, elle présente trois tons plats et quatre tons modulés. Les sept tons sont haut (H), moyen (M), bas (B), haut-bas (HB), moyen-bas (MB), bas-haut (BH) et bas-haut-bas (BHB). ... Les tons des termes lexicaux et grammaticaux sont invariables. Seuls quelques noms de parenté font exception. ... Des morphèmes tonals interviennent dans des processus de dérivation nominale et verbale. Les noms rédupliqués présentent souvent des inversions tonales. Une corrélation s'observe entre certains schèmes tonals, certaines catégories syntaxiques et certaines formes canoniques. Ainsi, les schèmes BH, HB, BHB n'affectent que des noms. Les verbes eux se répartissent selon les quatre schèmes B, H, M et MB. ... Les paires avancées dans le tableau 15 montrent que tous les schèmes s'opposent pour les monosyllabes.

audit.reasoning: (1) The deciding quotation is verbatim in the held HAL author's version of Fabre's Lincom reference grammar at the stated printed and PDF pages; the earlier A/B reader pair's verification reproduces. (2) The classification rests on the standard and only reference grammar of the language (2004, fieldwork-based, 485 pp), which is the best available description; Glottolog's other 'grammar' entries are the same work, and the remaining descriptive refs are a 1976 34-page phonology outline and Yaoundé morphosyntax theses. HAL shows no later phonological/prosodic publication by Fabre or others with a file; Lesage 2020 (downloaded) is a wordlist and silent. (3) The classification tonal-OR-pitch accent with domain not stated by the source correctly reflects that the grammar describes a 3-level lexical tone system and says nothing synchronic about stress (neither a rule nor a denial). Nothing seen suggests a stress system w

sources.citation: Essamba, Michèle (2002). Le Syntagme Nominal du Sámbá. Université de Yaoundé. Université de Yaoundé I. 126 pp.
sources.note: The catalog record for samba leko has an empty rule and no existing stress statements; this work is silent on stress placement. It does establish (as its §I.8.3, §II.3 and conclusion state) that the language is tonal with lexical and grammatical tone, which is consistent with the catalog having no stress rule but does not fill it.

sources.citation: Lesage, Jakob. 2020. Notes on Samba Leko as spoken in Donga. Unpublished ms., CNRS-LLACAN/INALCO, October 2020 version. HAL hal-05438562v1 (14 pp, CC BY-SA).
sources.quote: None. It is a tone-marked wordlist of the moribund Donga (Nigeria) variety with elicitation notes; a full-text search for stress/accent tone|stress|accent|prominence|pitch returns only the gloss 'stone'. Silent on word stress; transcriptions carry lexical tone marks consistent with a tone language.

sources.note: The only other phonology-typed description of Samba Leko (34 pp, Glottolog ref 52675; cited by Fabre p. 11 as the sole prior study). Our tonal coding rests on the grammar's silence about stress; Noss's outline is the one place an explicit statement on stress/accent (presence or absence) might exist, which could move the record from tonal-OR-pitch accent to an explicit no-stress or tone-plus-stress coding.
